summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, and a history of recurrent C. difficile infections was admitted for evaluation of anemia and reported rectal bleeding. Her hemoglobin had dropped from a baseline in the mid-30s to 21.0, prompting transfusion of two units of packed red blood cells. She was found to have internal hemorrhoids on colonoscopy, with a normal upper endoscopy, and the bleeding was attributed to either hemorrhoids or ongoing C. difficile colitis. She remained on oral vancomycin throughout the admission and showed stable hemoglobin levels by discharge. Her heart failure regimen was adjusted to metoprolol due to soft blood pressures, and aspirin was restarted. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and continue prescribed treatments.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Iron deficiency anemia secondary to blood loss (chronic)
